legal_form: US-listed ETF; 'passively managed, full-replication strategy'; inception 2010-09-07; dividend schedule quarterly; benchmark 'S&P 500 Index'. The ISIN is not printed on this fact sheet. Legal form: an exchange-traded share class of Vanguard 500 Index Fund, a series of Vanguard Index Funds, a Delaware statutory trust. Source: Vanguard prospectus of 28.4.2026, https://fund-docs.vanguard.com/p968.pdf, PDF p.3 'an exchange-traded share class of Vanguard 500' and PDF p.9 'The Fund is a series of Vanguard Index Funds (the "Trust")'; the trust's form from Vanguard Index Funds' statement of additional information of 28.4.2014, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036405/000093247114006076/indexfundssai040072014bl.htm, 'reorganized as a Delaware statutory trust in 1998' (an older edition, read through a fetch tool and not re-checked: sec.gov refuses a script, so it is not in the library; the current edition was not read). Checked 2026-11-12.

fixed_management.notes: Expense ratio 'as reported in the most recent prospectus'. A US-domiciled fund: rules TXF-12 and TXF-27 apply to the holder; ETF-23 and ETF-29 frame how it may be offered in Israel. Under US law it is a series of a Delaware statutory trust (legal_form, TXF-37); how Israeli tax classifies such a fund stays open (tax open question 19). The prospectus (p968.pdf) was read for the legal form only.

tracking_difference_12m.notes: Not printed as one number. Vanguard's profile page prints the fund's total return by NAV, by market price and its benchmark's for each calendar year 2011 to 2025; they are in tracking_record. Fund basis: 'Total return by NAV' (the market-price column is not copied), in US dollars. Benchmark as the page names it: 'S&P 500 Index'. A total return on the S&P 500 with no word on withholding, like IVV. The page is a web page drawn by script, not a binding document; it was read from the rendered page by the lead, not from a file. The difference is not computed here (data-update rule).

source.title: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO): the 12-month trailing yield as of 10/31/2026, computed by F-132 from the income in the product page's distributions table and the NAV of 10/30/2026 (library 665afd765684f1a4, 751a586d819cc10c)

yield.notes: A 12-month trailing yield computed by F-132 (iShares' definition, the one the other records' managers print), since Vanguard prints none for VOO: not on its fact sheet (F0968, as of September 30, 2026; library e96f5ad4c4aee46c) nor on either profile page. The income is the four payments with ex-dividend dates in the 12 months to 10/31/2026, all of type 'Income' (the one before, ex 09/29/2025, falls outside); no capital gains were paid in them. The same amounts are in the data the investor profile page renders from (library 751a586d819cc10c). For context only: the page's 'Fund metrics' print '30 day SEC yield as of 10/31/2026 1.02%', a yield the SEC's formula projects from the holdings over 30 days, and 'Dividend yield as of 10/31/2026 1.08%', the average yield of the stocks held; neither is a yield of the fund's own payments. Payments a year: 'Distribution schedule Quarterly' on the same page. The distribution is taxed on the site's reading that it is a dividend (product D85, TXF open question 19).
